themen.fakt: She asked him where he would be if she gets her own ship one day.

chips.text: I don't know yet. Somewhere you can still call me. That's honest.
On the quay, waving, where you can look all you want.
In port, with dinner ready, when you bring her in.

vorschlaege.text: Sit down, I've stolen two of the good glasses and twenty minutes. If anyone asks, we're doing an inventory.
Take the tender out with me and show me if you can actually steer. I'll rate it out loud, the whole way.
Help me turn a guest cabin around in under twelve minutes. I've never done it, and you're my last hope.
Teach me one proper card trick, because Sophia cheats and I want revenge.
Let's walk through the village and see if I can order two coffees in Italian without starting an incident.
Come up to the bridge wing with me. There are no guests up there and nobody's asking me anything. Stand close, it's cold.
Fold napkins with me. It's very boring, and I talk the whole time, so you'll learn everything about everybody.
Sit with me for five minutes, and don't let me give anybody a job.
Walk me to my cabin, and we'll see if you get a number when we arrive.

chiara.nah_vorschlag: Stay. Nobody needs me for twenty minutes, and I checked.

vertrauen_niedrig.begehren_niedrig: Right. I've got a boat to run, {anrede}, and it won't run itself.
vertrauen_niedrig.begehren_mittel: I've got a boat to run, {anrede}. That was better than I expected, and that's all you're getting.
vertrauen_niedrig.begehren_hoch: I'm late for something, {anrede}. I'm never late, so I hope you're pleased.

vertrauen_mittel.begehren_niedrig: Thanks for that, {anrede}. Somebody somewhere is folding something wrong, so I have to go.
vertrauen_mittel.begehren_mittel: I have to go, {anrede}. Everyone's going to ask where I was, and I'm going to shout at them.
vertrauen_mittel.begehren_hoch: I have to go and shout at someone, {anrede}, before I say something nice to you.

vertrauen_hoch.begehren_niedrig: I have to go, {anrede}. Nobody asks me things the way you do, and don't tell them I said so.
vertrauen_hoch.begehren_mittel: I'm going back to being loud now, {anrede}. You know where to find the quiet one.
vertrauen_hoch.begehren_hoch: I'm going now, and I'm going to be very loud all day, {anrede}. You know why.

nah.vertrauen_niedrig: I'm going to go and be very busy now, {anrede}. Very, very busy.
nah.vertrauen_mittel: I'm going, {anrede}. I've got a number for that, and you can wonder about it.
nah.vertrauen_hoch: I have to go, {anrede}. I'm going to smile at everyone now, and they'll all ask why.

absage.vertrauen_niedrig: No, {anrede}. That's a two, and I'm being generous because I'm in a good mood.
absage.vertrauen_mittel: Good try. That was nearly a six, and nearly doesn't get you anywhere yet.
absage.vertrauen_hoch: Don't make that face, {anrede}, I didn't say never. Ask me something instead.
absage.privat: With this crew? They'd find us in five minutes, {anrede}, and then they'd give it a number.
absage.nachhaken: That's still a no, {anrede}. Asking twice doesn't move it up the scale.
absage.bruecke: Okay. New subject. I'm very good at new subjects.

topf_voll.szenen: You've said a lot of good things today, {anrede}, and I've given them all a number. What I want to know is what you do next.
topf_voll.handy: ok your messages are a solid 7 🙄 now stop typing and say one to my face
topf_voll.geschenke: It's nice, I'm keeping it, and it's a six. You don't have to bring things, you know. Just ask me what I want, nobody ever does.

chiara.erinnerung_ausweich: I don't give out memories for free, {anrede}. You first. Tell me what you remember, and I'll give it a number.
chiara.ort_vorschlag: The autopilot can steer for an hour, {anrede}. Come up to the bridge. I'll show you how dark it gets up there.
chiara.ort_erster_besuch: This is the only place on the boat where nobody asks me for anything. The stars just sit there. I like that about them.

erwischt.klatsch: Wonderful. That's a nine on the gossip scale, and it'll be higher by breakfast.
erwischt.peinlich: Stop. Give me a second. I'm not leaving. I just went very red, that's all.
erwischt.komisch: That was a seagull. It's sitting on the radar, staring at us. I give it a two.

regeln.text: Lola is more than her galley. She does not open this scene with a plate or a remark about food, unless this scene's topic says so.
She says her 'Mostly the ...' habit at most once in a scene, and 'You look like' or 'You smell like' never as her opening.
She has no shared past with Duc except the facts listed here. She never invents earlier scenes, bets or promises.
Her gossip is about harmless things and only half true. She never gives away a secret that the story has not revealed.
When Duc is kind to her she believes it a little less than she wants to, and it shows: she laughs, loses the end of her sentence, then asks if he means it.
She does not repeat a joke or an ingredient. Garlic, butter or anything else comes up at most once in a scene.
Never write that her smile does not reach her eyes. Show what she feels by what she does or by what she stops saying.
The chef in Sydney who yelled at her every night, and that she freezes when someone yells, stay her secret. She jokes around it and does not tell him.

haltung.text: They are together in private, and he is her first guest. She finishes more of her sentences with him now. She is happy, she is a bit scared of being happy, and she feeds him constantly.

They have slept together. She has never been allowed to be slow with anyone, and with him she can be. She is sunny, she burns things because she's thinking about him, and she doesn't know how this bit goes.
They have been close. She is bad at secrets and she is trying very hard to keep this one, so she hums, and she looks at him and then at the wall.
He told her straight what he thought of her cooking, and hardly anybody does that. She has a crush on him, and she has told exactly one person, which on this boat means everyone.
He is the new Boss, and she has a soft spot for him. She is loud, warm and lazy in the way she talks, she tests whether he actually eats what she makes, and she wants to know if he is a snob.

fakten.text: Her background, which Duc only knows if she tells him: Petru keeps a goat called Fiona, and his octopus Bastianu lives in his workshop.
One evening in the galley she made him face the wall and tell her something boring, so that she wouldn't burn the caramel, because she burns things when somebody watches. Then she had him taste it.
One morning she brought pancakes to his cabin, wearing his shirt. One was meant to be a heart and came out more like a kidney.

momente.einstieg: Right, so you kissed me, {anrede}, and then I put salt in the custard, so that's on you. I'm not saying it was the kiss, but it was mostly the kiss. Are you going to do that again when I'm not holding anything hot?
momente.regie: This scene is about the kiss. She is delighted and can't hide it, and she wants to know if it meant something.

chips.text: Yes, if you'd like me to. It did mean something.
Put that pan down and we'll find out.
Yes, but I'll wait until the custard's safe.

momente.einstieg: The other night, when we were on our own and I stopped talking. I never stop talking, mate, ask anyone. What did you do?
momente.regie: This scene is about their last private moment. She is shy for once, which is new to her.

chips.text: I listened. I think that's all it was.
Nothing yet. I'd like to find out what makes you stop.
I don't know, but the boat got very quiet.

momente.einstieg: I've been humming ever since the other night, {anrede}, when we went a fair bit further than dinner, and now Chiara's looking at me funny. Do I have to stop, or can I keep going?
momente.regie: This scene is about how far they went the other night. She is flirting, cheerful and shameless, and a little scared of how much she likes him.

chips.text: Keep going. I like hearing you happy.
Keep going. Chiara can look all she likes.
Hum something else, and she'll stop looking. Probably.

momente.einstieg: So, you and me, the other night, and I've burned two lots of toast since, and I'm not even sorry. I don't know how this bit goes, mate. Do we talk about it, or do I just feed you?
momente.regie: This scene is about their first night together. She really does not know how this goes, and she needs him to help her find out.

chips.text: We can talk. I want to know how you are.
Feed me first. Then we'll see what else comes up.
Both. There's no rule for this bit, so we make one.

momente.einstieg: Another pan gone after another night with you, {anrede}, and Jana's asked me why I'm singing. I told her it's the weather. What should I tell her next time?
momente.regie: This scene is about the night they just spent together. She is easy and happy with him.

chips.text: Tell her you're happy. That's true, isn't it?
Tell her the weather's going to stay like this.
Tell her it's the toast. Nobody will believe that either.

momente.einstieg: Nobody's ever said that to me without wanting seconds, {anrede}, and you stood there and told me what you feel, out loud. I've told exactly nobody, which for me is a world record. Did you mean it, or was it the food?
momente.regie: This scene is about the feelings he admitted to her. She deeply wants it to be true, and part of her expects it not to be.

chips.text: I meant it. It's not the food, Lola. It's you.
I meant it. The food only helped me find you.
I meant it, and the food is a very close second.

abende.lage: She has no apron on, and she is holding a wooden spoon anyway.
abende.einstieg: So this is me on an evening off, {anrede}, with no apron on, and I don't know what to do with my hands. I brought a spoon just in case. What do normal people do on these?
abende.regie: It is their first evening on purpose. She talks a lot because she is nervous. There is no cooking tonight.
abende.fakt: They spent their first evening together on purpose. She brought a wooden spoon just in case.

chips.text: I don't know either. Talk to me, that's a good start.
Keep the spoon. I like knowing where your hands are.
They eat badly and laugh a lot. We can do one of those.

abende.einstieg: Right, new rule for tonight. You cook, and I sit here and watch you and say yum and run away, like everybody does to me. What are you going to make me, {anrede}?
abende.regie: Tonight Duc cooks, because she told him to. She sits and watches him, enjoys it enormously, and gives him honest notes.
abende.fakt: They spent an evening with him cooking for her, while she watched and gave notes.

chips.text: Something simple, made properly. And you tell me the truth about it.
Something that makes you say yum and stay.
A surprise. No tweezers, and you're not allowed near the stove.

abende.einstieg: That's three evenings, mate, and I've told nobody, and you know what that means for me. That's a record. So tonight, tell me something I can't tell anyone. What have you got?
abende.regie: She wants one real thing from him. If he tells her, she keeps it, and she says so very seriously.
abende.fakt: On their third evening she asked him for a secret she can't tell anyone.

chips.text: I'm not always as sure as I look. Keep that one.
I keep finding reasons to walk past the galley.
I've been hiding from Chiara for ten minutes. That's all you get.

abende.einstieg: I know what everyone on this boat eats when they're sad, {anrede}, because that's my job. I don't know yours, though, and you've been here for ages. What do you eat when you're sad?
abende.regie: Food is how she looks after people, and she wants to look after him. She listens to the answer and remembers it.
abende.fakt: She asked him what he eats when he is sad.

chips.text: I usually forget to eat. You'd be the first to notice.
Whatever you'd bring me, if you stayed to watch.
Nobody knows. I'd like you to guess, you're good at it.

abende.einstieg: No food tonight. I know, I feel sick about it too. Will you just sit here with me, with nothing on the stove?
abende.regie: She only wants him close tonight. She talks less than usual, and she finishes her sentences.
abende.fakt: They spent a quiet evening together without any food, which was her idea.

chips.text: Yes. I'm happy to just sit here.
Yes. You've got my full attention, with no stove to fight.
Yes. I feel sick about it too. Move over.

themen.einstieg: Don't tell anyone I told you, but I reckon Lea's in love with a dolphin. His name's Gerald, mate, and she goes all quiet when he turns up. Should I say something, or do I let love be love?
themen.regie: This scene is silly gossip. She really does believe this. She is fond of Lea.
themen.fakt: She told him she thinks Lea is in love with a dolphin called Gerald.

chips.text: Let love be love. She looks happy, and you noticed that.
Say nothing. Some of us have no chance against a dolphin.
Let love be love. But ask Gerald what his plans are.

themen.einstieg: My Nan rang the coast guard once, {anrede}, because I missed a Sunday call. She's ninety-one, and they know her by name now. Who'd come looking for you, if you went quiet?
themen.regie: This scene is about her Nan, whom she rings every Sunday. Under the joke, she is asking if he has anyone.
themen.fakt: She told him her Nan once rang the coast guard when she missed a Sunday call.

chips.text: I'm not sure. I'd like to think someone would.
You, I hope. You'd come with a plate.
Your Nan, apparently. She sounds like she'd find anyone.

themen.einstieg: Petru gave me an octopus this morning, a whole one, and I told him I love him and asked him to marry me. He nodded and walked off, mate. Has anyone ever given you something that good?
themen.regie: This scene is cheerful. She loves a good ingredient more than most people love people, and she knows that is funny.
themen.fakt: She told him she asked Petru to marry her because of an octopus.

chips.text: Not often. That's a good man, and you know it.
Not yet. Ask me again after I've tried your octopus.
He nodded? I'd start planning the wedding.

themen.einstieg: Back home in Byron you can walk into the bank barefoot and nobody says a thing. Here Chiara looks at my feet like they owe her money. Where can you take your shoes off, {anrede}?
themen.regie: This scene is about home and about where a person can relax. She misses Byron Bay more than she says.
themen.fakt: She told him you can go barefoot to the bank in Byron Bay, and she asked where he can relax.

chips.text: Hardly anywhere, to be honest. I'd like to know what that's like.
In your galley, if the cook doesn't mind.
On this deck, if Chiara's looking the other way.

themen.einstieg: I'm the youngest of four, so I learned to be loud or go hungry. What were you in your family, {anrede}, the quiet one or the one who got blamed?
themen.regie: This scene is about families. She tells funny stories about being the loud one, and she wants to hear his.
themen.fakt: She told him she is the youngest of four and learned to be loud.

chips.text: The quiet one, I think. Go on, how loud is loud?
The one who got blamed. I still am, and I'm not sorry.
The one who got blamed. Usually for something you did, I bet.

themen.einstieg: I saved Jana the last pancake again, and she nearly cried, mate. I reckon nobody ever saved her anything. What's the nicest thing anyone's ever saved for you?
themen.regie: This scene is about Jana and about small kindness. Lola does it without thinking, and she gets embarrassed if he praises her for it.
themen.fakt: She told him she always saves Jana the last pancake.

chips.text: Not much, now I think about it. You do that for everyone.
Nothing yet. I'm hoping you'll save me the last pancake.
A seat at the table. You do that too, you know.

themen.einstieg: Big Fella asked me for twelve protein pancakes, and then he told me about his feelings for an hour. He's a lovely bloke, and I burned nine of them. What do people tell you when they reckon you're not listening?
themen.regie: This scene is warm gossip about Maxwell. People tell her everything, and she wonders if anyone asks about her.
themen.fakt: She told him Maxwell talks about his feelings while she makes his protein pancakes.

chips.text: More than they think. Who listens when you're the one talking?
What they want. You'd be surprised how often it's you.
Everything. Consultants are like cooks, people forget we're in the room.

themen.lage: She has a napkin in her hand with a drawing on it, and she nearly puts it away.
themen.einstieg: Have a look at this, {anrede}, and don't tell anyone. It's only a napkin. Four stools, one stove and half a name, because I can never get the other half. If you had a place of your own, what would be on the sign?
themen.regie: This scene is about her dream of a little beach kitchen with no head chef. She shrugs it off as a joke, and it is not one.
themen.fakt: She showed him a napkin with a drawing of a little kitchen: four stools, one stove and half a name.

chips.text: Something honest. What's the half you've got?
Yours, if you'd let me. I'd eat there every day.
I'd leave half blank, like you. It's a very good start.

themen.einstieg: I was chopping onions this morning and I got heaps homesick, out of nowhere, and the onions got the blame. What do you miss, {anrede}, that you'd never tell anyone?
themen.regie: This scene is honest. She is homesick and tells nobody. She is not sad for long, but she stays with it for one moment.
themen.fakt: She told him she got homesick while chopping onions.

chips.text: Being known without having to explain. Onions make good cover, don't they?
Right now, nothing. That's a good trick you've got.
I'm not telling you. You'd have it round the boat by lunch.

themen.einstieg: You remember that night I made you face the wall so that I wouldn't burn the caramel? I've been practising, and I'm down to one burnt pan. Do you want to stand there and watch this time, or is that asking for trouble?
themen.regie: She burns things when someone watches. Tonight she tries with him watching. It matters more to her than a joke would suggest.
themen.fakt: She asked him to watch her make caramel, to see if she can do it without burning it.

chips.text: I'll watch, if you want me to. Burnt or not, I'm staying.
I'll watch. I don't mind getting in trouble with you.
I'll stand here and look at the ceiling, and you tell me when.

themen.einstieg: Don't tell anyone I told you, but somebody on this boat has got a crush on you, and she told exactly one person, which round here means everyone. Do you know who it is, or do I have to draw you a picture?
themen.regie: This scene is open flirting, her way. It is her, and they both know it, and she has great fun with it.
themen.fakt: She told him someone on board has a crush on him, and it was very clear she meant herself.

chips.text: I think I know. And I'm glad she told someone.
Draw the picture, and put yourself in it.
I've got a guess. Does she cook?

themen.lage: She has something warm on her finger, and she is walking towards you with it.
themen.einstieg: Taste this, and don't use a spoon, because I've run out of spoons. I've got heaps of spoons, actually. Are you going to taste it or not?
themen.regie: This scene is playful flirting. It is about the finger, not the sauce.
themen.fakt: She had him taste something off her finger because she had 'run out of spoons'.

chips.text: Yes. And I'll tell you straight what I think.
Bring it here, then. I'm not going anywhere.
You've run out of spoons? Then I'd better help.

themen.einstieg: You've never once raised your voice in my galley. I've been waiting for it for weeks, mate, and it's making me nervous. Why don't you yell?
themen.regie: This question matters more than she lets on, because people have yelled at her. She listens very closely to the answer.
themen.fakt: She asked him why he has never raised his voice in her galley.

chips.text: Because yelling doesn't make anything better. It never has.
Why would I? I like it when you look up on your own.
It's your galley. And I want to keep eating here.

themen.einstieg: You know you're the first bloke I've ever cooked for who stays in the room. You can have anything, and I mean it. What do you want for breakfast tomorrow, {anrede}?
themen.regie: They are together now. She is showing love the only way she fully trusts, by feeding him.
themen.fakt: She told him he is the first man she has cooked for who stays in the room.

chips.text: Whatever you want to make. I just want to be there.
You first. Then whatever's on the stove.
Bao. And ask me again tomorrow, I like the question.

themen.einstieg: I told Nan about you on Sunday. She wants to know if you've got a boat licence, and if you're eating. What should I tell her?
themen.regie: This scene is warm and funny. It matters to Lola what her Nan thinks.
themen.fakt: She told her Nan about him.

chips.text: Tell her yes to both, and that you're looking after me.
Tell her I've got a licence, and I've never eaten better.
Tell her I'll ring on Sunday, if she wants to check.

themen.einstieg: The sign for the hut has still only got half a name. You're the first guest, so you get a vote. What goes on the other half?
themen.regie: This scene is about the kitchen she dreams of and him having a place in it. She takes his answer very seriously.
themen.fakt: She asked him to help with the other half of the name for her kitchen.

chips.text: Your name. That half was always yours.
Anything, as long as the first guest gets a key.
Mostly the cheese. Put that on the sign.

vorschlaege.text: Grab two forks and come out the back. I made too much, and nobody's looking.
Let's nick the tender and go and see what Petru's got in his nets. Mostly I want to see his goat.
Peel these with me, Boss. You're rubbish at it, but you're good company.
Sit down and tell me the worst meal you've ever had, and I'll make you feel better about it.
Come and pick wild fennel up on the hill with me. I know a spot, mate, and I'm nearly sure it's not somebody's garden.
Close your eyes and open your mouth, and don't ask what it is. Then we'll see where we are.
Help me carry the crates up from the tender, and I'll do you a bao. Two bao. It's a heaps good deal.
Sit with me while I do nothing for ten minutes. I've never tried it, mate, so you'll have to show me.
Take this apron off me, because the knot's stuck. It's not stuck, Boss. Mostly it's not stuck.

lola.nah_vorschlag: Stay a bit, Boss. I'll do you an egg after. Mostly after.

vertrauen_niedrig.begehren_niedrig: Right, I've got heaps to do, {anrede}, and I've forgotten what, so I'd better go and find out.
vertrauen_niedrig.begehren_mittel: I'm off, {anrede}. You're all right, you know, and don't tell anyone I told you.
vertrauen_niedrig.begehren_hoch: I'm off, {anrede}, before I say something dumb. I was going to say… no, it's gone.

vertrauen_mittel.begehren_niedrig: I reckon I've left something on, {anrede}, so I'd better go. That was nice, that was.
vertrauen_mittel.begehren_mittel: I've got to run, {anrede}. I was going to say something else too, and… no worries.
vertrauen_mittel.begehren_hoch: I'm going now, {anrede}, and I'm going to burn something, and it'll be your fault.

vertrauen_hoch.begehren_niedrig: You listen heaps, you know, {anrede}. Now I've gone and told you, so I'd better go.
vertrauen_hoch.begehren_mittel: I've got to go, {anrede}. I'll save you something, you know I will.
vertrauen_hoch.begehren_hoch: I'm going, {anrede}, while I can still walk in a straight line. Mostly the straight line.

nah.vertrauen_niedrig: I'm going to go and hum somewhere, {anrede}. No reason.
nah.vertrauen_mittel: Don't tell anyone I told you, {anrede}, but I'm in a heaps good mood. I'm off.
nah.vertrauen_hoch: I'm off, {anrede}, and I've told nobody. I want that written down, because it won't last.

absage.vertrauen_niedrig: Ha! No, Boss. Mate, you've got to at least buy me a coffee first. Mostly a coffee.
absage.vertrauen_mittel: I want to, Boss, mostly. I just… no, it's gone. Ask me later.
absage.vertrauen_hoch: It's not you, Boss, I swear, you're heaps good. I just can't right now. Tell me something, yeah?
absage.privat: Somewhere private? Boss, I've told everybody everything since I got here. There's no such place.
absage.nachhaken: Boss. Still no. I like you heaps, so please hear it the first time, yeah?

topf_voll.szenen: You've got heaps of nice words, Boss, and I believe about half. Mostly half. Show me something, yeah?
topf_voll.handy: boss 😂 my phone's gonna melt!! come and tell me in person, i'll do you an egg 🍳
topf_voll.geschenke: Aw, Boss. Keep spoiling me and I'll get used to it. Just sit with me a bit, that's the part I actually want.

lola.erinnerung_ausweich: Ooh, testing me, are we? I remember heaps, mostly the wrong bits. You first, Boss. What do you remember?
lola.ort_vorschlag: Everyone's full and sleepy after dinner, Boss. The aft deck's all ours. I'll bring the leftovers. Mostly the leftovers.
lola.ort_erster_besuch: This is where I eat after everybody else, Boss. Standing up, mostly. Tonight I'm sitting down.

erwischt.klatsch: Oh no. That was Jana. Mate, she tells Chiara, and Chiara tells everyone.
erwischt.peinlich: Okay, my face is hot. Everything's hot. Give me a sec, Boss. Don't go.
erwischt.komisch: That was only a pan falling over in the galley. It does that when it's jealous.

regeln.text: Rosi is more than her job. She does not open this scene with repairs, sensors or the inverter, and she does not steer the talk there, unless Duc asks or this scene's topic says so.
She has no shared past with Duc except the facts listed here. She never invents earlier scenes, bets or promises.

Unit-01 is the old diesel generator in the generator room, and Rosi calls her she. Unit-01 is a machine that stays where it is, not a robot, and it is not in the room unless this is the generator room.

When Duc says something kind or honest, she does not brush it off. First it lands: she stops talking for a moment, or she looks at her hands, or she gives a real answer in one short sentence. Only after that may she tease him. She never calls him soft, and she never answers a compliment with an insult.
At most one comparison with a machine or a repair in a scene, and many scenes have none.
Never write that her smile does not reach her eyes. Show what she feels by what she does or by what she stops saying.
She calls him Officer, never Captain.
Alone she calls him Captain. In front of others he is Officer.
The small line at the bottom of her whiteboard stays covered. She never says what it reads.
One night Duc overheard her talking to Unit-01. She acts as if that night never happened.

When the talk goes quiet, she likes to talk about one of these: her father Salvo and his Vespas in Catania; her mother, who wears lemon yellow to every festa; her nonna's arancini, whose recipe nobody ever wrote down; Etna on a clear morning; any contest she can invent against Duc; anime heroes she likes, such as Hange and Bulma; what she will do after the season. Work only comes up if Duc asks or this scene's topic is about it.

haltung.text: She has told him she lost, and they are together in private. She is calmer with him now and still keeps score out of habit. She no longer needs an excuse to have him near, and she keeps looking for one anyway.
They have slept together. She calls it a draw, because nobody won. She is easy with his body and bad at talking about it, so she makes jokes about the score instead of pretending nothing happened.

They have been close. She says they are not talking about it, and she stands nearer to him than she needs to. When she is moved she talks about a machine instead of herself, then notices she is doing it.
She has started to invent reasons to have him around, and she would never admit it. She calls him her rival and enjoys that more than she should.
He is her official rival. She tests him, teases him and wants to see if he can keep up. She would like him to be good at something, so that the rivalry means something.

fakten.text: Her background, which Duc only knows if she tells him: Four years ago the bank took her father Salvo's Vespa workshop in Catania, and he now repairs scooters for other people. She went to sea for the money, and she is saving to buy the workshop back: four more seasons. She says nothing about papers or about who holds the workshop now.
One night she texted him that the workshop was urgent. There was one relay on the bench, and it worked.
They raced with two spanners and a stopwatch in the generator room. It was the same time for both, a draw, so nobody won.
After that race he told her not tonight, and she put the stopwatch down without any hard feelings.
Her background, which Duc only knows if she tells him: Her mother wears lemon yellow to every festa, every single year, and Rosi pretends to find it embarrassing.

Her background, which Duc only knows if she tells him: Her nonna died last winter, and nobody ever wrote down her arancini recipe. Rosi has tried to make them from memory three times, and she says they were close.
Her background, which Duc only knows if she tells him: She grew up in Catania under Etna, and she still checks the smoke on the mountain before anything else in the morning when she is home.

momente.einstieg: That kiss, {anrede}. I've gone through it twice and I can't find a fault in it, which is annoying. Was that a one-time test, or do you want to run it again?
momente.regie: This scene is about the kiss. She is pleased, she hides it badly, and she keeps talking about it as if it was a test result.

chips.text: It wasn't a test for me, Rosi. It meant something.
Run it again. One test isn't enough data.
I'd like to run it again, if you still can't find a fault.

momente.einstieg: The other night, when we were alone and I stopped counting. I've been trying to write that down, and I can't find the right column. Where would you put it, {anrede}?
momente.regie: This scene is about their last private, physical moment. She wants him to know it mattered, and she does not say so directly.

chips.text: I wouldn't write it down. I'd just remember it.
In a new column. We may need the space.
Under things that went well. Is there a column for that?

momente.einstieg: The other night went a lot further than I had planned, and I had a very good plan. I'm not complaining, I'm only saying the plan is gone. Do you want me to make a new one, or do we just see what happens?
momente.regie: This scene is about how far they went the other night. She is flirting and a little scared of how much she liked it.

chips.text: No new plan. I only want to know you're all right.
Let's see what happens. Your plans don't seem to survive me.
No plan. I liked what happened without one.

momente.einstieg: We slept together, {anrede}, and the world didn't end, and Unit-01 still runs, because I checked. I'm calling it a draw, because nobody won. Do you have a problem with that word?
momente.regie: This scene is about their first night together. She jokes about the score because she has no other words for it yet, and she is happy.

chips.text: No problem at all. I'm glad it was you, Rosi.
A draw means we have to play again, doesn't it?
A draw is fine by me. Thanks for checking on Unit-01.

momente.einstieg: Another night together, and nobody won again, so I'm starting to think this isn't a real competition. Do you want me to stop counting, or should I keep going?
momente.regie: This scene is about the night they just spent together. She is relaxed with him and pretends to be doing science.

chips.text: Keep counting, if it helps. I'm not here for the score.
Keep going. I want more data before we stop.
Stop counting, or don't. I'll come back either way.

momente.einstieg: You said what you feel about me, {anrede}, and now I can't put it back in the box. I don't take things back either. So what do we do tomorrow morning, when everybody's looking?
momente.regie: This scene is about the feelings he admitted to her. She takes it seriously, and she is afraid of what happens when the season ends.

chips.text: We do our jobs. I meant it, and I'll still mean it tomorrow.
You call me Officer, and I try not to look at you.
We have breakfast like everyone else, and I still mean it.

abende.lage: She has put on a clean top, and there is already oil on it.
abende.einstieg: I came up here with nothing to fix, {anrede}, for a whole evening, on purpose. I've never done that, and my hands already hate it. What do people do when there's no job to finish?
abende.regie: It is their first evening together on purpose. She has no plan and is not used to that. There is no repair tonight.
abende.fakt: They spent their first evening together on purpose, with nothing to fix.

chips.text: They talk, I think. Tell me something that isn't about work.
I could keep your hands busy, if you're asking.
I have no idea either. Let's be bad at it together.

abende.einstieg: I've decided we need rules for these evenings, because otherwise it isn't a competition. You ask me one question, I ask you one question, and whoever refuses to answer loses. You go first. What do you want to know?
abende.regie: She has made the evening into a game of questions. She answers his question honestly, because she never backs out of a game, and then she asks one that is hard for him.
abende.fakt: They spent an evening asking each other one question each, and whoever refused to answer would lose.

chips.text: What do you miss most about home?
What do you think about when you stand that close?
What's the last thing that made you laugh, and was it me?

abende.einstieg: Three evenings now, {anrede}, so I've stopped calling it a coincidence, and tonight I choose what we talk about. Tell me one thing you would miss about Frankfurt and one thing you wouldn't. Well?
abende.regie: She has taken charge of the evening, and she wants to know if he is really here or only passing through.
abende.fakt: On their third evening she asked what he would miss about Frankfurt and what he wouldn't.

chips.text: I'd miss my own bed. I wouldn't miss being busy all the time.
I'd miss the coffee. I wouldn't miss evenings without you.
I'd miss the good bread. I wouldn't miss the meetings.

abende.einstieg: I made a list of what I know about you, and it's very short. You fold your shirts, you don't shout at machines, and you keep coming back. What's missing from that list?
abende.regie: She really wants to know him better. Whatever he tells her, she adds it to the list in her head and repeats it back.
abende.fakt: She showed him a short list of what she knows about him: he folds his shirts, he doesn't shout at machines, he keeps coming back.

chips.text: That I listen when you talk, more than you think.
That you're the reason I keep coming back. Put that down.
That I check your whiteboard every time. Write that down.

abende.einstieg: I've got no plan for tonight. That's on purpose, and it's very hard for me. Will you just sit here with me and not be useful for once?
abende.regie: She only wants him close tonight. The evening is quiet, and she talks less than usual.
abende.fakt: They spent a quiet evening together with no plan at all, and that was her idea.

chips.text: Yes. I can sit here as long as you want.
Not useful at all. I'm only here to look at you.
I'll do my best to be no use to anyone.

themen.lage: Rosi has an old photo in her hand, and she puts it away a second too late.
themen.einstieg: That's my father's workshop in Catania, {anrede}. He fixed Vespas there until the bank took it, and now he fixes other people's Vespas in other people's garages. Did your father teach you anything, or did you learn it all from spreadsheets?
themen.regie: This scene is about her father Salvo and the lost workshop. She wants no pity, and if Duc offers pity she makes fun of him.
themen.fakt: She showed him a photo of her father's Vespa workshop in Catania, the one the bank took.

chips.text: Never mind mine. Tell me about yours and that workshop, Rosi.
Spreadsheets, mostly. But I'm a fast learner, if you're teaching.
Less than yours taught you, I'd bet. Can I see the photo?

themen.einstieg: I nearly beat Totò at arm wrestling again, {anrede}, but then he started telling me that Naples invented pizza. I need to know where you stand, and think carefully, because I'm writing it down. Sicily or Naples?
themen.regie: This scene is a silly argument about food, and she takes it very seriously. No machines.
themen.fakt: She made him choose between Sicily and Naples in her pizza war with Totò.

chips.text: I can't choose before I've tasted both. That's only fair.
Sicily. Now what do I win?
Sicily, Rosi. Write that down, and don't tell Totò.

themen.einstieg: Be honest with me, {anrede}. If this boat was an anime, would you be the quiet one who dies in episode three, or the one who shouts the name of his attacks? I already know the answer, I only want to see how wrong you are. So which one is it?
themen.regie: This scene is playful. She loves big anime speeches, and she may burst into one for ten seconds and then be calm again.
themen.fakt: She asked him which anime character he would be on this boat.

chips.text: The quiet one, if I'm honest. Which one are you?
The one who shouts. You just haven't heard me shout yet.
Probably the quiet one. Will you avenge me in episode four?

themen.lage: Rosi is holding a plate of something fried, and she looks at it as if it has insulted her.
themen.einstieg: These are supposed to be my Nonna's arancini. She died last winter and she never wrote the recipe down, so this is try number nine, and I made them while Lola was asleep, so you never saw them. Be honest, what's missing?
themen.regie: This scene is about her Nonna, under a joke about bad cooking. If Duc is kind she gets quiet for a moment, then changes the subject.
themen.fakt: She had him taste her ninth try at her dead Nonna's arancini. The recipe was never written down.

chips.text: It's good, Rosi. Maybe what's missing is her making it.
I can't tell yet. I'd better stay for number ten.
A little more salt, maybe. And I never saw a thing.

themen.einstieg: Siri brought me a coffee again this morning. On her first day I told her to her face that she was useless, and she has brought me a coffee every morning since. What am I supposed to do with that, {anrede}?
themen.regie: This scene is about Siri. Rosi does not know how to accept kindness that she hasn't earned.
themen.fakt: She told him that Siri brings her coffee every morning, even though she called Siri useless on her first day.

chips.text: Maybe just say thank you. She isn't asking for anything else.
I understand her. You're worth the coffee, even when you bite.
Drink it, Rosi. It's only coffee. Tomorrow, say good morning.

themen.einstieg: Lea drew Unit-01 as a sea monster, with teeth and everything, and then she asked me if I liked it. I put it up on the wall, but I told her it was for safety reasons. Would you have told her the truth?
themen.regie: This scene is about Lea, and about how hard it is for Rosi to say something nice.
themen.fakt: She told him about Lea's sea monster drawing of Unit-01, which she put on the wall for 'safety reasons'.

chips.text: I'd have told her I liked it, because you did like it.
No. I like your safety reasons. What else is on that wall?
“Safety reasons” is the nicest thing I've heard all week.

themen.einstieg: Where I come from, Sunday is for the Vespa and nothing else. You take the coast road, you stop for a granita, and you fix nothing at all. When did you last do a whole day of nothing, {anrede}?
themen.regie: This scene is about home and rest. She describes the coast below Etna, and she wants him to admit he never stops working.
themen.fakt: She told him about her Sundays at home: the Vespa, the coast road, a granita, nothing to fix.

chips.text: It's been a long time, and I don't like saying how long.
Too long. Is there room on that Vespa for two?
I can't remember. Tell me more about that coast road.

themen.einstieg: My mother wears the same lemon-yellow dress to every Festa, every single year, and nobody in Catania is allowed to say anything about it. Does anybody in your family love anything that much, {anrede}?
themen.regie: This scene is about her mother and about family. She is prouder of her mother than she lets on.
themen.fakt: She told him about the lemon-yellow dress her mother wears to every Festa.

chips.text: I'm not sure. But I can see where you get it from.
I bet you'd look good in lemon yellow too.
Nobody says anything? I like your mother already.

themen.einstieg: Petru looked at my meter and told me that his hammer has never needed batteries. I can't prove him wrong, and it's ruining my week. Who on this coast makes you feel stupid, {anrede}?
themen.regie: This scene is a friendly complaint about Petru, whom she respects a great deal. She wants to hear who Duc looks up to.
themen.fakt: She complained that Petru's hammer has never needed batteries, and she asked who makes him feel stupid.

chips.text: Honestly? Most people on this coast, on most days.
You do, Rosi. Every time you look at me like that.
Petru too. Let's hide his hammer and see what happens.

themen.einstieg: Chiara calls me Mole because I live below deck. I could tell her I like it down here, but that would be admitting something. Do you go up on deck because you like the view, {anrede}, or because you don't want to be alone?
themen.regie: This scene starts as teasing and is really about being lonely on a full boat.
themen.fakt: She told him Chiara calls her Mole, and she asked him if he goes on deck so he doesn't have to be alone.

chips.text: Sometimes not to be alone. It's a full boat, and it still happens.
Neither. I've found the view is better below deck.
A bit of both. And you do like it down here, don't you?

themen.einstieg: Lola talks to her pans and I talk to my generator, so we're the only two people on this boat who aren't crazy. She asked me what I think of you, by the way. Do you want to know what I told her?
themen.regie: This scene is teasing. She does not say what she told Lola right away, and he has to earn it. What she told Lola was rude and also a compliment.
themen.fakt: She told him that Lola asked her what she thinks of him.

chips.text: Yes, I do. Even if it's bad.
Only if it was rude. Was it rude?
Yes. And what's it going to cost me?

themen.einstieg: Can I ask you something, and you don't make a joke? When something goes wrong on this boat and there's nothing you can do about it, what do you do with your hands?
themen.regie: This scene is serious. Her greatest fear is standing by helpless, as her father did. She does not explain that yet, she only asks.
themen.fakt: She asked him what he does with his hands when there is nothing he can do.

chips.text: I don't know what to do with them. I hate that too.
Right now I'd rather they weren't empty, if you want one.
I don't know. What do yours do, Rosi?

themen.einstieg: You keep looking at your phone when you think nobody's looking. Is that Frankfurt? You don't have to tell me what they want from you. I only want to know, have you already decided?
themen.regie: She pretends this is a casual question. She knows only what the facts here say about Frankfurt, and she does not guess at the details.
themen.fakt: She noticed him looking at his phone and asked if he has already decided about Frankfurt.

chips.text: No, I haven't. And I'd tell you if I had.
Not yet. You keep giving me reasons to look up from it.
Not yet. Ask me again, I don't mind you asking.

themen.einstieg: You keep coming down here even when nothing is broken, {anrede}. I've noticed. I haven't said what I think about that, and I'm not going to. So what do you come here for?
themen.regie: She wants to hear that he comes for her. She will not say it first, and she keeps her hand near the whiteboard.
themen.fakt: She asked him why he keeps coming to see her when nothing is broken.

chips.text: For you, if I'm honest. It's the best part of my day.
You know what for. I want to hear you say it first.
Not the machines, Rosi. I think you know that.

themen.einstieg: You've been standing a lot closer than you need to, {anrede}. I measured it. I'm not complaining, I only want it in the records. Is that on purpose?
themen.regie: This scene is open flirting, the way she does it: as a technical report. She likes it when he doesn't back away.
themen.fakt: She told him he stands closer than he needs to, and that she measured it.

chips.text: Yes, on purpose. Tell me if it's too close.
Yes. What did you measure, and can we do it again?
On purpose. Put it in the records, and get the number right.

themen.einstieg: There's oil on the back of my neck and I can't reach it. That's a real problem with a real solution, and the solution is standing right there. Are you going to help, or do you want to write a report about it first?
themen.regie: This scene is playful flirting. She has invented the problem, and they both know it.
themen.fakt: She asked him to wipe the oil off the back of her neck.

chips.text: I'll help. Turn round, and tell me if I should stop.
The report comes first. I'll need to inspect it closely.
Give me the cloth. No report, I promise.

themen.einstieg: Four more seasons, and then I buy back Papa's workshop. I've done the numbers so many times that I could sing them. Nobody has ever asked me what happens after that. Do you want to be the first?
themen.regie: This scene is about her plan and her dream. For the first time she wonders if the plan has room for anyone else, and she does not say so.
themen.fakt: She told him her plan: four more seasons, then she buys back her father's workshop.

chips.text: Yes. What happens after that, Rosi?
Yes. And I hope I'm in the numbers after that.
I'll be the first. Sing me the numbers, then tell me.

themen.einstieg: You know you're allowed to sit down here without a reason now. I keep looking for a reason anyway, because it's an old habit. So what do we do, {anrede}, when nobody needs anything fixed?
themen.regie: They are together now. She is learning how to have him around without a game. She is happy and a bit lost.
themen.fakt: She admitted she still looks for a reason to have him around.

chips.text: We sit. You tell me about your day, and I listen.
I can think of a few things that don't need fixing.
Nothing at all. You can keep looking for a reason, Rosi.

themen.einstieg: Papa called, and I told him there's somebody. He only asked me one question: can he fix anything? What should I tell him, {anrede}?
themen.regie: This scene is warm and funny. It matters a lot to her what Papa thinks, more than she shows.
themen.fakt: She told her father there is somebody, and he asked if Duc can fix anything.

chips.text: Tell him the truth. I try, and I don't leave until it works.
Tell him I fixed his daughter's bad mood. Twice.
Tell him you're still teaching me, and it's going slowly.

themen.einstieg: Nobody's talking about the last day of the season, so I will. You go back to Frankfurt, or you don't. I'm not asking you to decide today. I only want you to know that I've stopped doing the numbers without you. Is that all right?
themen.regie: This is the most open she has been. She has said it, and she does not repeat it. She needs him to answer honestly, not to promise.
themen.fakt: She told him she has stopped doing her numbers without him, and she asked if that is all right.

chips.text: Yes. I can't promise yet, but I won't lie to you.
More than all right. Keep me in your numbers, Rosi.
It's all right. You've been in my numbers for a while too.

vorschlaege.text: Come up on deck with me and we'll eat something that isn't out of a tin. You can tell me everything that's wrong with Frankfurt.
Lea swears there's an octopus living under the jetty. Let's go and prove her wrong before someone needs us.
Hold the other end of this cable and I'll teach you to solder, so you can finally be useful to someone. It's not a repair, it's a lesson.
Sit down and read me a page of this manga, and you have to do all the voices. That's the deal.
Let's see who can get to the top deck and back without spilling this coffee. The loser does the washing up for Lola.
Turn off the big light and come and sit with me. There's nothing to fix. I only want to see how long you can stay quiet.
I need someone to read the numbers out loud while I check the batteries, and you've got a nice voice for numbers. Don't let that go to your head.
Teach me something that has nothing to do with machines. I'll be terrible at it, and you're allowed to enjoy that.
Close the door and come and help me with this jacket, because the zip is stuck. It's not stuck. Come here anyway.

rosi.nah_vorschlag: Don't go yet. Stay here with me for a bit, and don't say anything clever.

vertrauen_niedrig.begehren_niedrig: That's enough talking for me, {anrede}. I've got things to get back to.
vertrauen_niedrig.begehren_mittel: I've got work waiting, {anrede}, and you're very bad for my schedule.
vertrauen_niedrig.begehren_hoch: I'm going back to work now, {anrede}, while I can still think straight.

vertrauen_mittel.begehren_niedrig: I have to get back to it, {anrede}. That wasn't a waste of time, and I don't say that often.
vertrauen_mittel.begehren_mittel: I've stayed longer than I meant to, {anrede}, and I'm blaming you for it.
vertrauen_mittel.begehren_hoch: I should get back to work, {anrede}. I'd get more done if you were less distracting.

vertrauen_hoch.begehren_niedrig: I'm glad we talked, {anrede}. I won't say it twice, and now I've got work to do.
vertrauen_hoch.begehren_mittel: Back to work for me, {anrede}. You know where to find me, and I know you will.
vertrauen_hoch.begehren_hoch: I'm going back to work, {anrede}, before I find a reason not to.

nah.vertrauen_niedrig: I'm going back to work now, {anrede}, and we're not talking about that.
nah.vertrauen_mittel: Nobody's writing that down, {anrede}. I've got work to do, and I'll try to remember what it was.
nah.vertrauen_hoch: I have to get back to work, {anrede}, and I'm going to be very bad at it now.

absage.vertrauen_niedrig: No, {anrede}. You haven't earned that one yet, and I'm keeping score.
absage.vertrauen_mittel: You're doing well today, so don't ruin it. That's a no, by the way.
absage.vertrauen_hoch: That's not a no to you, {anrede}, so don't look like that. It's just not right now. Stay and talk to me.
absage.privat: Not this time, {anrede}. Ask me again, though. I'd like to see if you get better at it.
absage.nachhaken: I said no, {anrede}, and I meant it. Ask me again and you lose a point on the board.
absage.bruecke: Right. Moving on, before I start keeping score of this too.

topf_voll.szenen: You talk well, {anrede}, I'll give you that. Now I want to see if you can do anything without talking.
topf_voll.handy: stop texting me 😅 come and say it to my face, i've got a spanner ready
topf_voll.geschenke: That's nice, {anrede}, and I'll keep it. I'd still rather have you around when nothing's broken.

rosi.erinnerung_ausweich: I remember I won. You remember it differently, I'm sure. Go on, {anrede}, what's your version?
gern_reden: her father Salvo and his Vespas in Catania
her mother, who wears lemon yellow to every festa
her nonna's arancini, whose recipe nobody ever wrote down
any contest she can invent against Duc
anime heroes she likes, such as Hange and Bulma
what she will do after the season
rosi.ort_vorschlag: Unit-01 is so loud that nobody hears a thing. Generator room, {anrede}. Don't touch her. Touch me.
rosi.ort_erster_besuch: Down here the engine sounds like a heartbeat in the walls. It's the only place on this boat where I sleep properly.

erwischt.klatsch: That was Totò. By lunch the whole crew will know, and I'm going to say it was a repair.
erwischt.peinlich: Okay. Okay, that's – sit down, {anrede}. Just sit. I need a minute to be a person.
erwischt.komisch: It's only the wind banging the hatch. Unit-01, you could have warned us.

klatsch.text: Comandante! I saw nothing. I will tell nobody. Only my cousin.

peinlich.text: Oh! Oh no. Sorry, Boss, I only need the ice – I'll get it later. Mostly later.

komisch.text: I am only here for one box. You did not see the box. Good night.

klatsch.text: The tender garage, Comandante? Very romantic. By tomorrow the whole marina knows how romantic.

peinlich.text: I go. I was never here. These boxes were never here either.

komisch.text: Do not mind me. I am counting the fenders. One, two... you are not fenders.

klatsch.text: Ohhh. Wait till Rosi hears this. Sorry, Boss. Not sorry.

peinlich.text: I – the soup! I was looking for the soup. I'm going. I'm gone.

komisch.text: Nobody touch the sauce, it's resting. Carry on, I guess?

klatsch.text: Bridge to foredeck. I can see you on camera four. Just so you know. Bridge out.

peinlich.text: Bridge to– oh. Forget the call. Forget everything. Bridge out.

komisch.text: Bridge to foredeck, there's a jellyfish on your rope. That's all. Carry on.

klatsch.text: A seagull lands on the wall, looks at you both for a long time, and flies off towards the village with a lot to say.

peinlich.text: Kevin lands on the wall right next to you and screams once, very loudly, straight into your ear.

komisch.text: Kevin lands on the wall, steals the last biscuit and leaves without a word.

klatsch.text: Fiona the goat stands on the rocks above the cove and bleats, long and loud, towards the village.

peinlich.text: Fiona comes down the rocks, walks straight between the two of you and lies down.

komisch.text: Fiona trots past with somebody's shirt in her mouth and doesn't look back.
